body.statement: Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and a positive certificate. Use \(\operatorname{vec}_H=(\iota_C,\iota_Y)\), the \(k_Y\times m_H\) Jacobian \(J_H\), \(\operatorname{IF}_H(c)=J_H(\mathbf p_H)(e_c^C-\mathbf p_H)\), and \(\Sigma_H=\operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\operatorname{IF}_H(V,S)\}\). At every fixed \(p_H\) in the differentiable interior of its branch-specific \(\mathfrak D_H\), \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\), and \(F_H(\widehat p_H)\) is asymptotically linear on the on-domain event. For fixed \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), set \(\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}F_H(\widehat p_H)\), \(\widehat v_{H,y}=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_H e_y^Y\), and \(CI_y=[\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}/n}]\). If \(\Sigma_H\{\iota_Y(y),\iota_Y(y)\}>0\), then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.\] For fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), use the defined \(CI_{\lambda}\); then \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_{\lambda}\}=1-\alpha.\] Thus the coverage targets are respectively the single component \(Q_{a,H}(y)\) and the fixed scalar contrast \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\), each pointwise at the fixed interior law. On the off-domain event the procedure returns \(\bot_H\) and no confidence set; no positivity-boundary-uniform coverage is claimed.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a positive certificate and \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), put \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\), and suppose that \(\mathbf p_H\) lies in the differentiable interior of the branch domain \(\mathfrak D_H\).  Let \(C=\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\).  The finite-alphabet assumption makes \(m_H=|C|<\infty\), and for \(X_i=(V_i,S_i)\),
\[
 \widehat{\mathbf p}_H=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n e_{X_i}^C,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{p_H}(e_{X_i}^C)=\mathbf p_H.
\tag{1}
\]
The domain is described by finitely many strict inequalities in coordinates and registered polynomials, all continuous.  Interiority therefore supplies a relative neighborhood \(N\) of \(\mathbf p_H\) in the simplex and \(\delta>0\) such that the relative \(\ell_\infty\)-ball of radius \(\delta\) lies in \(N\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  Since
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H(c)\}
 =\frac{p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}}{n},
\]
coordinatewise Chebyshev inequalities and a finite union bound give
\[
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\notin N\}
 \le
 \frac1{n\delta^2}\sum_{c\in C}p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\).

All registered denominators are positive on a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(\mathbf p_H\).  The finite rational circuit \(F_H\) consequently has a continuously differentiable ambient-coordinate extension there.  Differentiability, (1), and the bound
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_H}\left\|\sqrt n
 (\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)\right\|_2^2
 =\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)
 -\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}<\infty
\]
give, on the event in (2),
\[
 F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)
 =J_H(\mathbf p_H)(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)
 +o_p(n^{-1/2})
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{IF}_H(X_i)+o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{3}
\]
The influence function has mean zero by (1), and it has finite variance because \(C\) is finite.  The same differentiability expansion along every interior multinomial submodel proves regularity of this local smooth plug-in.  Therefore \(\textnormal{lem:asymptotic-linear-normality}\), applied after premultiplication by a fixed \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_Y}\), yields
\[
 \sqrt n\,c^{\mathsf T}
 \{F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)\}
 \rightsquigarrow
 N\bigl(0,c^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Hc\bigr).
\tag{4}
\]

On the reporting event, direct expansion of the defined empirical influence functions gives
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H
 =J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 -\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\widehat{\mathbf p}_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{5}
\]
The empirical table converges in probability to \(\mathbf p_H\) by (2), and the Jacobian of a rational circuit is continuous where its registered denominators are nonzero.  Hence
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H\longrightarrow
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)-\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)^{\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_H
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{6}
\]
The last equality follows by taking the variance of the influence function in (3).

Certificate soundness gives \(F_H(p_H)=Q_{a,H}\).  Fix \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\) and take \(c=e_y^Y\) in (4).  If
\[
 v_{H,y}:=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H e_y^Y>0,
\]
then (6) implies \(\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}\to1\) in probability and \(\Pr(\widehat v_{H,y}>0)\to1\).  Thus
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)-Q_{a,H}(y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}}}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1).
\tag{7}
\]
For clarity, the studentization in (7) follows directly from (4) and (6): on \(\{|\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}-1|\le\varepsilon\}\), compare the statistic with the two fixed rescalings by \((1\pm\varepsilon)^{-1/2}\), use continuity of the normal distribution function, and then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).  The quantile definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\), (2), and (7) now imply
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]

For a fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), take \(c=\lambda\) in (4) and premultiply (6) by \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda\).  The identical comparison argument gives
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_\lambda\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) concern respectively one fixed outcome component and one fixed scalar contrast.  Off \(\mathfrak D_H\), the procedure returns \(\bot_H\) and reports no interval.  Since the neighborhood in (2) depends on the fixed interior law, the proof makes no claim of uniform coverage as a cell probability or registered denominator approaches zero.
body.justification: The statistical rung turns every positive graphical certificate into an estimable finite-table causal functional.
body.gap: Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser derive inference for fixing functionals, but not for one joint fixed-support selector table generated by the proposed complete calculus.
body.consumer: Applied users of a selector-aware dosearch backend obtain point estimates, standard errors, and pointwise Wald intervals from the same returned circuit.
